title: The woman and the dragon (Revelation 12)
hookLine: a woman clothed with the sun, a dragon, and a child snatched up to safety

lines: A WOMAN CLOTHED WITH THE SUN.
A DRAGON WAITS AT THE BIRTH.
THE CHILD IS CAUGHT UP TO GOD.
cards: "And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars." She's in labor, crying out.
Then a second sign: a great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, its tail sweeping stars from the sky. It waits in front of her, ready to devour the baby the moment it's born.
The child comes, and before the dragon can move, the child is caught up to God and to his throne. The woman runs into the wilderness, to a place God has prepared for her.

teach.b: First, who is she? Revelation gives her no name tag, and Christians read her more than one way.
Catholic tradition sees in her Mary, the mother of the child who rules, and also the church; Orthodox writers have read her both ways too.
Some Protestant readers see God's people: Israel, who brought the Messiah into the world, and the church that follows. Some hold all of these at once.

Second, the "war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon." And the dragon "prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven." He's thrown down, and named: that old serpent, the devil.
Third, how he's beaten. Not by a bigger dragon. The faithful "overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony."

teach.h: BEATEN BY THE LAMB AND THE TRUTH.
teach.b: A slain Lamb and people telling the truth. Fourth, the earth helps.
The dragon pours a flood from its mouth to sweep the woman away, and "the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood." The ground itself takes her side.
For all its monsters, the chapter keeps its eye on a mother. Every time she appears, she's in danger: she runs, she hides, she's chased. And she's kept.
The dragon doesn't get the child, and it doesn't get her.

how: Catholic Christians hear Revelation 12 read on feasts of Mary, and Christian art has pictured her clothed with the sun and crowned with stars; some Protestant preachers read it as the story of God's people kept safe in trouble.

games.q: what does “the woman and the dragon” mean?
o: Revelation 12's mother and child threatened by a dragon
a vision in Daniel of four beasts rising from the sea
a fairy tale of a knight who rescues a captive princess

games.q: the woman and the dragon — tap the pairs.
p: clothed with the sun, crowned with stars
caught up to God and his throne

s: Revelation names the woman as Mary
it never names her. Catholic and Orthodox tradition sees Mary and the church; some Protestants see Israel and the church.
the earth itself helps the woman
"the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood."
the dragon is beaten by a bigger monster
"they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony."

games.q: you're the woman. your child has been caught up to God, and the dragon has turned on you. what do you do?
o: stand and fight the dragon alone.
run into the wilderness, to a place God has prepared.
games.why: she flees into the wilderness, where a place has been prepared for her. when the dragon sends a flood, the earth swallows it.

practice: Hold in mind mothers running with their children right now, from war, from a violent home, from hunger, and one woman giving birth tonight with no one safe beside her.
If someone you know is carrying a child or a family alone, hold her by name, and if you pray, ask that she be given a place prepared, like the woman in the wilderness.
If you're the one who isn't safe at home, you deserve safety: call local emergency help, or in the US, call or text 988.

wordCard.voice: The woman and the dragon. Revelation twelve's picture of a mother and her child under threat, a dragon thrown down, and a woman kept safe in the wilderness.

orig.note: Greek: dragon, a great serpent. Revelation 12 calls him that old serpent, the devil.

carryVoice: Your line: the dragon loses. Not to a bigger dragon, but to a Lamb. Until tomorrow.
